question.text: As part of the daily verification of the time-stamping machine log at an RTA / collection centre, which control check must be performed every morning?

answer.text: The machine's battery level and calibration status
The number of applications that missed the cut-off time on the previous day
Verify that the first time-stamp serial number issued in the morning continues from the last time-stamp serial number of the previous day
Only the total number of transactions processed during the previous day

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook control requires that every morning the first time-stamp serial number issued is verified against the last time-stamp serial number issued at the close of the previous day. This continuity check ensures no serial numbers have been skipped or fabricated between the two business days. The Trap: "First and last serial numbers issued the same day" only confirms in-day completeness; it does not detect tampering between days. Battery / calibration checks and miss-the-cut-off counts are operational monitoring items, not the prescribed serial-number continuity control. Note: A full daily control report typically captures the first serial number of the day, the last serial number of the day and the cut-off-time serial number separately, so that pre-cut-off and post-cut-off applications can be reconciled.
